title: The id Field Is a Promise to Reply

questions.question: What is the one thing that determines whether a JSON-RPC message expects a response?
options: Whether the message itself includes a non-null id field
Whether the method name starts with the word notifications
Whether the message is sent over HTTP instead of stdio
Whether the server happens to recognize the method being called
questions.explanation: A JSON-RPC message is a request when it carries an id and a notification when it does not; that single field, not the transport or the method name, decides whether any response follows.

questions.question: A client sends notifications/initialized to a server right after reading the initialize response. What does the server do with it?
options: Send back a result confirming the notification was received
Send back an error because the method name is unfamiliar
Process it if the method is recognized, and send nothing back
Queue it and reply once the next request arrives later
questions.explanation: A notification carries no id, so nothing is owed back under any circumstance; a server that recognizes notifications/initialized simply treats it as informational and moves on without sending a reply.

questions.question: A request names a JSON-RPC method the server has never implemented. Which response is correct?
options: A result payload containing an empty object as a placeholder
An error with code -32601, keyed to the request id
A response with no result and no error at all
Silence, since an unfamiliar method never gets answered at all
questions.explanation: A request always receives exactly one response; when the method itself is not implemented, that response is a JSON-RPC error whose code identifies the method as unknown, not a silent drop or an empty success.

questions.question: Which primitive is designed so that a user, not the model, decides when it runs?
options: A tool, since the model chooses it based on the task
A resource, since the host attaches it without being asked
The protocol version, since it is fixed before any request
A prompt, since the user selects it through the host
questions.explanation: Prompts are built for explicit user selection, commonly through a slash command or menu, while a tool is chosen by the model and a resource is attached by the host or application on the caller's behalf.

questions.question: The demo server receives tools/call for add with only one of its two required arguments. What happens?
options: The server returns an INVALID_PARAMS error naming the missing argument
The server instead returns a METHOD_NOT_FOUND error for the call
The handler runs anyway, treating the missing value as zero
The server silently drops it, since it carries an id
questions.explanation: The tool's own input schema lists both arguments as required, so the dispatcher rejects the call before the handler ever executes, using the invalid params code reserved for bad arguments to an otherwise known method.

questions.question: Two requests are in flight on the same connection, id 3 and id 4. A response arrives with id 4. How does the client know which call it answers?
options: It answers whichever request happened to be sent first in time
It answers the pending request with the lowest outstanding id
It answers the one pending request whose own id also equals 4
It answers every pending request outstanding on that connection
questions.explanation: A response repeats the id of the request it answers, so a client with several calls outstanding on one connection matches each reply to its own pending call by that shared id, never by arrival order or count.
